themes.mechanism: Light values on :root; dark values via @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) on :root:not([data-theme="light"]) and on :root[data-theme="dark"]. The override is persisted in localStorage key 'vagas-theme'.

title.purpose: Open job title in the side panel; empty-state heading.

headline.purpose: Row titles (15px on mobile), scores, brand name.

body.purpose: Default text; section heads at 600; descriptions at 1.6 line-height, 75ch max.

body-small.purpose: Top-bar meta, row AI summary, field grids, segmented control.

label.purpose: Labels, counts, row meta, captions, menu titles, list sub-heads. Sentence case.

shadows.name: overlay
shadows.purpose: Menus, toasts, and the side panel as a drawer below 1012px. Nothing else.

motion.name: ease-out-expo
motion.purpose: Entrance easing for panel, menus and toasts.

motion.name: state-change
motion.purpose: Button background and card border transitions.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: All animation and transition durations under prefers-reduced-motion.

breakpoints.name: drawer
breakpoints.purpose: At or below: side panel becomes a fixed overlay drawer.

breakpoints.name: mobile
breakpoints.purpose: At or below: wrapped top bar, 16px padding, no row checkboxes or summaries, short button labels, full-width panel.

narrative.overview:
Vagas is GitHub Issues/Projects rendered in Primer, with no metaphor laid over it. The user chose the category standard deliberately: every job is an issue, every status is an issue state, the AI verdict is a label, and the list is the product. Nothing on the page is decoration; a color, icon or border exists because Primer would put it there and because it carries a state.

The surface is dense and quiet. Neutral canvases and 1px borders carry the structure; hue appears only in state icons, labels, scores and the one blue for links and focus. Light and dark themes follow the OS through `prefers-color-scheme` and can be pinned with a `data-theme` override on the root, both using Primer's own values. Motion is brief and functional: panels slide in, menus drop in, toasts rise, and all of it collapses under `prefers-reduced-motion`.

Rejected by the user during the world choice: the metaphorical worlds (post-office sorting hall, work-booklet, arcade and the rest). The category's conventions stay as GitHub ships them.
keyCharacteristics: Primer neutrals, light and dark, with a `data-theme` override.
Status and verdict colors live only in state icons, labels and scores.
System UI stack at 14px with tabular numerals throughout.
6px radius, 1px borders, flat surfaces; shadows only on overlays.
Octicons 16px, `currentColor`, as the only icon set.

rules.name: The Status Color Law
rules.body: Status colors map to GitHub issue semantics and never drift: `nova` = success green (issue-opened), `interessante` = attention yellow (star), `aplicada` = done purple (check-circle), `entrevista` = accent blue (comment-discussion), `encerrada` = muted gray (issue-closed), `descartada` = muted gray (skip). AI verdicts: `forte` = success label, `avaliar` = attention label, everything else (`fila`, `descartar`, `sem`) = outline label.

rules.name: The Not-Planned Rule
rules.body: Descartada is gray, like GitHub's "closed as not planned": discarding is archiving, not an error. Red is reserved for the Descartar button and for errors.

rules.name: The Labels-Only Rule
rules.body: Semantic hue appears only as a state icon, a label, a score, or a banner tint. Surfaces, headers and columns stay neutral.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` is set on the body; every score, count and date aligns in columns.

rules.name: The Sentence-Case Rule
rules.body: Labels, tabs, headings and sub-heads are sentence case in pt-BR. No uppercase tracking.

rules.name: The Overlay-Only Rule
rules.body: A shadow means "this floats". Rows, cards, boxes, columns and buttons never carry one; hover is shown by fill or border change.

dos: **Do** follow the Status Color Law exactly; a new status gets a GitHub-meaningful Octicon and one semantic hue.
**Do** keep Descartada gray and reserve `danger` red for the Descartar button and errors.
**Do** read every color from the custom properties so light, dark and the `data-theme` override stay in sync.
**Do** use Octicons at 16px with `fill: currentColor` for every icon.
**Do** keep surfaces flat with 1px borders and 6px radius; shadows go on menus, toasts and drawers only.
**Do** use the system UI stack at 14px with tabular numerals.
donts: **Don't** put semantic hue on surfaces, headers or columns; it belongs in icons, labels, scores and banners.
**Don't** add a metaphor, custom display face or decorative illustration; the category standard is the chosen world.
**Don't** hard-code colors that bypass the theme variables.
**Don't** use a shadow to show hover or selection on rows, cards or buttons.
